channel.title: Brume Updates
channel.description: New versions of Brume, the macOS terminal reimagined.

item.title: Version 0.1.0
item.description:
Added

  • A terminal built on the Ghostty engine: tabs in the top bar or in a vertical sidebar, split terminals grouped inside a tab, search, text zoom, and your windows and tabs restored on relaunch.
  • Tabs with a name, a color and an icon, reordered by dragging, with ⌘1 to ⌘9 shown while ⌘ is held.
  • A badge on each tab that follows Claude Code and long commands: progress, finished, bell, and red when a command failed.
  • When Brume is in the background, a notification tells you when Claude Code is waiting or a long command finishes; click it to jump to the terminal. The Dock icon shows how many terminals need a look. Both can be turned off in Settings › General.
  • Command highlighting, suggestions from history and a Tab completion menu, on by default.
  • Settings inside the window: glass effect, 10 accent colors, 12 fonts, 16 command color palettes, English and French (Brume follows your Mac's language on first launch).
  • A welcome screen in every new terminal: a pixel-art visual tinted with your accent color, a word in large letters, and your Mac's information.
  • Full Path in Tabs (Settings › General) shows a tab's folder from your home folder, like ~/Desktop/project, instead of its name alone. Renamed tabs keep their name.
  • Keyboard shortcuts you can change in Settings › Shortcuts, for tabs, terminals and vertical tabs, with a warning when a combination is already taken.
  • ⌃Tab and ⌃⇧Tab switch tabs, Clear Screen (⌘K) in the Edit menu, and a Help menu with links to Brume on GitHub and to report an issue.
  • A confirmation before closing a terminal where a command is still running.
  • Drop files or folders from Finder onto a terminal to type their paths at the cursor, escaped for the shell. In a split tab, they go to the terminal under the pointer. Dropped text is pasted as is.
  • Open a folder in Brume: drop it on the Dock icon, use open -a Brume <folder>, or right-click it in Finder › Services › New Brume Tab Here.
  • ⌘-click a file path like src/App.vue:42:5 to open it at that line in your editor, relative to the terminal's folder. A folder opens in Finder.
  • While a program asks for a password (sudo, ssh), Brume turns on secure input so other apps can't read what you type, shown by a small lock.
  • Reset Window (⌥⌘R, or Settings › General) brings a window back to a single tab with default names, colors and size, after a confirmation. Your settings are kept.
  • SSH sessions keep working with servers that don't know Ghostty's terminal type.
  • An app icon and a DMG to install Brume by dragging it to Applications.
  • Automatic updates, and a button to check for updates in Settings › General.

Fixed

  • With vertical tabs on, a new window opens wider to make room for the sidebar, so the terminal and its welcome screen keep their full size.
